subject.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout

question: Should a timed-out but uncancellable Discord listener retain its concurrency slot indefinitely, accepting bounded queue growth or event drops if it never settles?
rationale: The patch correctly enforces actual listener concurrency, but it intentionally changes the timeout failure mode from excess background work to persistent backpressure, which is an operator-visible availability tradeoff.

options.title: Accept bounded backpressure
options.body: Keep the patch semantics and require live proof that timeout metrics, queue saturation, late rejection handling, and recovery behave as intended.

options.title: Add cooperative cancellation
options.body: Extend the listener contract with an abort signal and release the slot only after confirmed cancellation or settlement, which is broader and requires listener-owner follow-through.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep current timeout-throughput behavior until maintainers define whether `listenerTimeout` prioritizes continued dispatch or strict actual-work concurrency.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded backpressure
recommendation.body: Keep the patch semantics and require live proof that timeout metrics, queue saturation, late rejection handling, and recovery behave as intended.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related Discord timeout-boundary work is the closest available history signal for deciding the intended queue failure semantics.
